newsitem.title: FRANCE: Shell halts Berre chemical unit but blockade eases.
newsitem.headline: Shell halts Berre chemical unit but blockade eases.

text.p: French truckers partially lifted a blockade against the Royal Dutch/Shell oil and chemicals complex at Berre on Friday, but not before plant managers were forced to shut virtually all chemical output due to the effects of the 12-day strike, a plant official said.
A blockade of the refinery part of the complex was continuing, however, but the company scrapped plans to reduce output there because the strike was starting to weaken, he said.
"The lorries have left from the chemicals area but we stopped almost all the chemical production units last night and today," the official told Reuters.
The shutdown was necessary because stocks were full.
Chemical production will be restored from Monday, he said.
The Berre plant near Marseille, France's third largest refinery, was one of the first major oil plants to be hit by truckers' blockades aimed at preventing fuel deliveries by road.
The Shell official said the company had drawn up plans to slow down refinery production from the end of this week if the strike continued, but these no longer seemed necesssary.
Shell was ready to get petrol moving from the refinery over the weekend if the lorries parked in front of loading ramps were driven away in time, he said.

The national road traffic centre said roadblocks were disappearing fast across France on Friday afternoon after truck drivers' unions ended talks with employers reporting substantial progress on pay and working hours.
